subject: AI & Agents
title: Which Jobs Will AI Replace?
description: A 60-second lesson on Which Jobs Will AI Replace?.

hook.text: Goldman Sachs predicts 300 million jobs will be affected by AI automation. Affected, not eliminated.

buildup.text: AI automates tasks, not entire jobs. Most jobs are bundles of tasks, some automatable, some not.

discovery.text: Routine, repetitive tasks go first — data entry, basic analysis, scheduling.

twist.text: Creative and social tasks were supposed to be safe. Then AI started writing and creating art.

climax.text: The safest jobs require physical dexterity, emotional intelligence, and novel problem-solving.

punchline.text: AI won't replace you. Someone using AI might.

quiz.question: What types of tasks does AI automate first?

details.summary: AI is most likely to automate routine cognitive tasks: data entry, basic analysis, and pattern matching. Jobs requiring empathy, physical dexterity, and complex judgment face lower automation risk.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding which jobs are at risk helps workers and educators prepare. The impact will be uneven across industries, skill levels, and geographies.
takeaways: Routine cognitive tasks face the highest automation risk
Creative and empathetic roles are harder to automate
The impact varies significantly across industries and regions

faq.question: Which specific jobs are most at risk from AI?
faq.answer: Data entry clerks, bookkeepers, basic customer service agents, and routine document reviewers face high risk. Jobs requiring creative thinking, emotional intelligence, and physical adaptability are safer.

faq.question: Will AI create new jobs to replace the ones it eliminates?
faq.answer: Historically, technology creates new roles. AI is generating demand for prompt engineers, AI trainers, ethicists, and data curators. The challenge is ensuring displaced workers can transition.
